So as, tho it were a year or more after the Birth of Chirst, before these Wise Men came, yet it is possible they might find him at <ns0:hi>Bethlehem,</ns0:hi> his Parents being as Guests there, tho Inhabitants at <ns0:hi>Nazareth.</ns0:hi> This is enough to have spoken of the time when these Wise Men came, <ns0:hi>viz.</ns0:hi> At what distance from the Birth of <ns0:hi>M<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                           <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>y,</ns0:hi> considering that nothing can be in the Case certainly determined: It is yet a greater Question, who these <ns0:hi>Wise Men</ns0:hi> were, and from what part of the World (here called the <ns0:hi>East</ns0:hi>) they came. The incertainties of mens Conclusions in their points of Curiosity, rather than profit, let us know how vainly Men search for satisfaction, when God hath hidden a thing from them. They cannot agree in the number of these men, some will have them twelve, some but three, and they undertake to tell us their Names, tho neither can they agree in it: Some will have them to be <ns0:hi>Kings,</ns0:hi> and the <ns0:hi>Papists</ns0:hi> make us believe they have their Sepulchers with them to this day at <ns0:hi>Cologne</ns0:hi>; and by the number of the Tombs they know their number, and that Church hath a Festival for them (which is our twelfth day) these and an hundred more Fa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bles there are about them. The Scripture saith no more than <ns0:hi>Wise M<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>n,</ns0:hi> and telleth us nothing of their number, whether they were meer <ns0:hi>Astrologers,</ns0:hi> or such as were skilled in <ns0:hi>magical Arts,</ns0:hi> or more generally <ns0:hi>Philosophers,</ns0:hi> is vainly Disputed, only we have their observation of this extraordinary Star, together, with what the Scripture tells us of the use those Eastern Na<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tions made of <ns0:hi>Astrologers,</ns0:hi> to guide us to think, they were such as were Famous in their Country, for <ns0:hi>Astrology</ns0:hi>: Tho others think them Persons skilled in <ns0:hi>Divine,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Humane</ns0:hi> Laws. The Scripture only calls them <ns0:hi>Wise Men.</ns0:hi> Whether they came from the Eastern parts of the World, or that part of the World which lay <ns0:hi>Eastward</ns0:hi> to the <ns0:hi>City of Ierusalem,</ns0:hi> is another unprofitable Question; <ns0:hi>Pagans</ns0:hi> they were without doubt, whether <ns0:hi>Persians</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Arabians,</ns0:hi> or of some other Country, is of no great Concern for us to know, and almost impossible to determine. These were the first Fruits of the Gentiles owning <ns0:hi>Christ</ns0:hi> as <ns0:hi>King of the Iews,</ns0:hi> whilst he came amongst his own, and they received him not: Nor do I know any thing more worthy of our observation concerning them, those that think it worth the while to read what more is said concerning them, may read enough in <ns0:hi>Spanhem</ns0:hi> his <ns0:hi>Dub. Evang. Heinsius</ns0:hi> his <ns0:hi>exercitat.</ns0:hi> Sac and <ns0:hi>Poli Critica</ns0:hi> which I rather chuse to name than the <ns0:hi>Popish Writers,</ns0:hi> because in some of these he will find the <ns0:hi>Antidote</ns0:hi> together with the <ns0:hi>Poison</ns0:hi> of those Fa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bulous Discourses, and be taught a Pious wariness of obtru<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ding old Wives Fables into <ns0:hi>Canonical</ns0:hi> History, and lightly im<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />posing upon the Faith of ignorant People.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="2">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:220" />2 Saying, where is he that is born King of the Jews? for we have seen <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Num. 24.17.</ns0:note> his Star in the East, and are come to worship him.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Ierusalem</ns0:hi> was the <ns0:hi>Metropolis of Iudea,</ns0:hi> thither they come, as to the most likely place, where to receive satisfaction. Of whom they inquired the Scripture saith not, but it is observable that they took notice that there was a Person born, who was to be an <ns0:hi>Illustrious King</ns0:hi> of the Jewish Nation, they speak not at all doubtfully as to that. This Information they doubtless had from a <ns0:hi>Divine Revelation,</ns0:hi> for altho there was an extraordi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nary <ns0:hi>Star</ns0:hi> appeared, which might let them know that God had produced, or was producing so extraordinary a work of Provi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dence in the World, yet without a supernatural Interpreter, they could not have made so true and particular Interpretation of it, as upon the sight of it to have come with such a Confidence to <ns0:hi>Ierusalem,</ns0:hi> affirming that there was a <ns0:hi>King of the Iews</ns0:hi> born, and that this was his <ns0:hi>Star,</ns0:hi> a <ns0:hi>Light</ns0:hi> which God had put forth to direct that part of the World, to the true <ns0:hi>Messiah</ns0:hi>: All guesses at the Nature of this Star, and the means how the <ns0:hi>Wise Men</ns0:hi> came to know that the <ns0:hi>King of the Iews</ns0:hi> was born upon the sight of it, and its motion, are great incertainties, God un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />doubtedly revealed the thing unto them, and caused this extra<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ordinary <ns0:hi>Star</ns0:hi> as at first to appear, to confirm what he told them, so at last to appear directing them to the very House in which the young Child with his mother were [<ns0:hi>and are come to Wor<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ship him</ns0:hi>] whether <ns0:hi>Worshipping</ns0:hi> here signifieth only a <ns0:hi>Civil Honour,</ns0:hi> which those <ns0:hi>Eastern Nations</ns0:hi> ordinarily gave unto great <ns0:hi>Princes,</ns0:hi> or that <ns0:hi>Religious Homage</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Adoration</ns0:hi> which was due unto the <ns0:hi>Messias,</ns0:hi> is variously opened by Interpreters, it is said, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 11. they <ns0:hi>fell down and Worshipped him,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>when they had opened their Treasures,</ns0:hi> they <ns0:hi>presented unto him Gifts, Gold, Frankincense, and Myrrh.</ns0:hi> This might be upon a <ns0:hi>Civil</ns0:hi> or upon a <ns0:hi>Religious Account</ns0:hi>; and doubtless was ac<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cording to the <ns0:hi>Revelation,</ns0:hi> which they had, concerning which nothing can be certainly determined.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="3">3 When Herod the King heard <ns0:hi>these things,</ns0:hi> he was troubled, and all Jerusalem with him.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Herod</ns0:hi> was hardly warm in his Kingdom, and had taken <ns0:hi>Ieru<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />salem</ns0:hi> by Force, and was therefore much concerned, to hear that there was a <ns0:hi>new King</ns0:hi> born, and supposing him to have been all his Life acquainted with the Jewish Writings and Records where were Prophecies of the <ns0:hi>Messias,</ns0:hi> under the Notion of a <ns0:hi>King</ns0:hi> and not knowing that the Kingdom of the <ns0:hi>Messias,</ns0:hi> was not to <ns0:hi>be of this World,</ns0:hi> but being possessed of the or<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dinary Notion of the <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> that the <ns0:hi>Messias</ns0:hi> should restore a <ns0:hi>Temporal Kingdom to Israel,</ns0:hi> he could not but be troubled at the News of one born, who was to be the <ns0:hi>King of the Iews,</ns0:hi> especially having a Confirmation of it by such an extraordinary means, as Persons coming from a far Country, and being di<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rected to their Journey by some extraordinary impulse, upon the sight of a <ns0:hi>new Star</ns0:hi>; which pointed to <ns0:hi>Iudea,</ns0:hi> as the place to which it related; <ns0:hi>Herod</ns0:hi> upon this might justly think that his newly acquired<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> Kingdom would not last long. And tho most People are quickly weary of Conquerors, yet their former miseries being fresh in their minds, and the renewing of them likely upon a Change in the Government, it is no wonder if the generality of the People, were also troubled.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="4">4 And when he had gathered all the chief Priests and Scribes of the people together, he de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />manded of them, where Christ should be born.<ns0:note place="bottom">In this Perplexity the King <ns0:hi>Herod</ns0:hi> calleth a <ns0:hi>Synod</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Convo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cation,</ns0:hi> which was made up of the chief <ns0:hi>Priests,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Scribes,</ns0:hi> the single Question which he propoundeth to them, was to resolve him. <ns0:hi>Where Christ should be born.</ns0:hi> It is most likely this was an extraordinary Convention of such of these Persons as the King thought fit, who were best skilled in the <ns0:hi>Law,</ns0:hi> and other <ns0:hi>Revelations</ns0:hi> of <ns0:hi>Holy-writ,</ns0:hi> not any orderly meeting of the <ns0:hi>Sanhedrim,</ns0:hi> for the Question propounded to them was of meer <ns0:hi>Ecclesiastical Concern</ns0:hi>: and to be resolved from the <ns0:hi>Pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />phecies</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Writings</ns0:hi> of the Old Testament. The stating of the <ns0:hi>Question</ns0:hi> to them, not <ns0:hi>Where the King of the Iews,</ns0:hi> but where Christ <ns0:hi>should be born,</ns0:hi> makes it manifest, that altho (that we read of) the Wise Men said nothing of <ns0:hi>Christ,</ns0:hi> yet <ns0:hi>Herod</ns0:hi> presently conceived, that this <ns0:hi>King of the Iews,</ns0:hi> that was born, must be the <ns0:hi>Messiah</ns0:hi> Prophecied of <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 2. and in <ns0:hi>Dan.</ns0:hi> 9. he therefore desired to know of them the place, in which accord<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing to their received Tradition, and Sense of the Prophecies of Holy-writ, the <ns0:hi>Messiah</ns0:hi> whom they expected (that is <ns0:hi>Christ</ns0:hi>) should be born.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="5">5 And they said unto him in Bethlehem of Ju<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dea for thus it is written by the Prophet.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="6">6 And thou Bethlehem <ns0:hi>in</ns0:hi> the land of Judah, art not the least <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Joh. 7.4.</ns0:note> amongst the Princes of Judah: for out of thee shall come a Governour that shall <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                        <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>.</ns0:note> rule my people Israel.<ns0:note place="bottom">It was (as it seems) so received a Tradition, and Interpreta<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion of <ns0:hi>Micah.</ns0:hi> 5.2. that they gave him an Answer without any Hesitation, telling him. <ns0:hi>He was to be born in Bethle<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />hem of Iudea,</ns0:hi> this they confirm by the Prophecy of the Pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />phet <ns0:hi>Micah ch.</ns0:hi> 5. <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 2. So confirming the Son of the <ns0:hi>Virgin Mary</ns0:hi> (at unawares) to be the <ns0:hi>Messiah</ns0:hi> from the Testimony of the Prophet <ns0:hi>Micah.</ns0:hi> The words in <ns0:hi>Micah</ns0:hi> something vary from those here mentioned, they are thus. <ns0:hi>But thou, Bethlehem Ephrata, tho thou be little amongst the Thou<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sands of Iudah, yet out of thee shall come forth unto me, one that is to be Ruler of Israel whose goings forth have been of Old from Everlastings.</ns0:hi> We must know that the Writers of the <ns0:hi>New Testament</ns0:hi> in their Quotations out of the <ns0:hi>Old Testament,</ns0:hi> ordinarily quote only so much of them as make to their purpose, and not always in the very terms in which they are found in the Old Testament, but keeping to the Sense. 2. That it is more than probable that the <ns0:hi>Evan<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gelist</ns0:hi> keeps to the words, in which the Priests and Scribes de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />livered in their Answer to the King, for in this Relation he is but reciting their Answer. The sole Question propounded to them was, <ns0:hi>What the place was where the Messiah according to their Records was to be born?</ns0:hi> They Answer in <ns0:hi>Bethle<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />hem Iudah,</ns0:hi> they prove their Answer from the Testimony of the Prophet. If any object that the Prophet calls it <ns0:hi>Bethlehem Ephrata</ns0:hi> not <ns0:hi>Bethlehem Iudah.</ns0:hi> The answer is, that it is in Sense the same, for <ns0:hi>Bethlehem Ephrata</ns0:hi> was within the Tribe of <ns0:hi>Iudah,</ns0:hi> it should seem by <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 35.19. and 48.7. that it was former<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly in <ns0:hi>Iacobs</ns0:hi> time called <ns0:hi>Ephrah,</ns0:hi> some think that it was a Town within <ns0:hi>Calebs</ns0:hi> portion, and called <ns0:hi>Ephratah</ns0:hi> from his second wife, whose name was <ns0:hi>Ephrah,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Ephratah,</ns0:hi> 1 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 2.19.50. if it were not the same place only fortified anew. We read of an<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />other <ns0:hi>Bethlehem</ns0:hi> in <ns0:hi>Iudah</ns0:hi> builded by <ns0:hi>Rehoboam,</ns0:hi> 2 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 11.6. whether it had this Addition, from its old Name, in <ns0:hi>Iacobs</ns0:hi> time, or from <ns0:hi>Calebs</ns0:hi> Wife, or to distinguish it from <ns0:hi>Bethlehem,</ns0:hi> belonging to the Tribe of <ns0:hi>Zabulon</ns0:hi> is hard to say, it is plain, that that <ns0:hi>Bethlehem</ns0:hi> is meant both by <ns0:hi>Micah</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Mathew,</ns0:hi> which was in <ns0:hi>Iudah,</ns0:hi> possibly in Tract of time the Addition <ns0:hi>Epratah</ns0:hi> was lost, but say some there is a Contra<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />diction betwixt, <ns0:hi>Micah</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Mathew, Micah</ns0:hi> saith it was the least, <ns0:hi>Mathew</ns0:hi> saith <ns0:hi>it was not the least. Ans.</ns0:hi> Here is no Contradiction, consider <ns0:hi>Bethlehem</ns0:hi> it self, it was but a small City (if it were in <ns0:hi>Calebs</ns0:hi> Lot, it is not named) but in other respects it was not the least. It was of old, Famous for <ns0:hi>Ibza<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>
                     </ns0:hi> one of the <ns0:hi>Iudges,</ns0:hi> for <ns0:hi>Elimelech, Boaz, Iesse, David,</ns0:hi> and now last of all for the Birth of Christ with respect to which the <ns0:hi>Evangelist</ns0:hi> calls it <ns0:hi>not the least,</ns0:hi> or if he reciteth the <ns0:hi>Scribes</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Priests</ns0:hi> words, they might call it <ns0:hi>not the least</ns0:hi> up<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on the account of <ns0:hi>Boaz, Iesse</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>David,</ns0:hi> all which were born or dwelt there; and particularly with respect to Christ, who was born there: The <ns0:hi>Prophet</ns0:hi> calls it the least with respect to its State in his time, the <ns0:hi>Evangelist</ns0:hi> not the <ns0:hi>least</ns0:hi> with respect to its State then, its State being magnified by the Birth of Christ. <ns0:hi>Micah</ns0:hi> saith amongst the <ns0:hi>Thousands, Mathew</ns0:hi> amongst the <ns0:hi>Princes.</ns0:hi> It is the same thing for <ns0:hi>Num.</ns0:hi> 1.16. their Princes were <ns0:hi>Heads</ns0:hi> of <ns0:hi>Thousands</ns0:hi> in <ns0:hi>Israel.</ns0:hi> The <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> would by no means have their Text interpreted of Christ, but either of <ns0:hi>Zoro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />babel</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>David,</ns0:hi> but as to <ns0:hi>Zorobabel</ns0:hi> he was born in <ns0:hi>Babylon</ns0:hi> not in <ns0:hi>Bethlehem,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> was dead long before this Prophecy, neither could the following words [<ns0:hi>whose goings forth have been old</ns0:hi> even from <ns0:hi>Everlasting</ns0:hi>] agree to <ns0:hi>Zorobabel,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Da<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vid: Zorobabels</ns0:hi> name tells us where he was born, and we ne<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ver read that <ns0:hi>Bethlehem</ns0:hi> was thus celebrated with reference to <ns0:hi>David,</ns0:hi> tho he was born there, 1 <ns0:hi>Sam.</ns0:hi> 16.1. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 17.58. upon which account it is called the City of <ns0:hi>David, Luk.</ns0:hi> 2.4. The Prophecy certainly related to Christ, and him only, and so is interpreted by the <ns0:hi>Chaldee Paraphrast,</ns0:hi> who some think was one of this Councel called by <ns0:hi>Herod</ns0:hi> in this Cause.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="7">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:220" />7 Then Herod when he had privily called the wise men enquired of them diligently what time the star appeared.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Herod</ns0:hi> having heard the Answer of the <ns0:hi>Priests</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Scribes,</ns0:hi> did not think fit to make any noise of it amongst the People, he knew the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> were apt enough to <ns0:hi>rebel,</ns0:hi> and being so late a Conqueror had no reason to presume much of their good Will towards him, he therefore calls the <ns0:hi>Wise Men privily,</ns0:hi> and takes no notice of any <ns0:hi>King</ns0:hi> they talkt of, but only inquireth the time, <ns0:hi>When this new Star first appeared,</ns0:hi> to what end he made this inquiry, may be learned from <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 16. only that he might be able to Govern himself in his bloody Decree, that he might neither destroy more Children than would serve his present Design, nor yet leave this Child behind.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="8">8 And he sent them to Bethlehem and said, Go, and search diligently for the young child, and and when you have found <ns0:hi>him</ns0:hi> bring me word a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gain that I may come and worship him also.<ns0:note place="bottom">He tells the <ns0:hi>Wise Men,</ns0:hi> that <ns0:hi>Bethlehem</ns0:hi> was the place, wherein his Wise Men had informed him, that the <ns0:hi>King of the Iews was to be born,</ns0:hi> and sends them thither with these Instructions: That they should <ns0:hi>go,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>search diligently</ns0:hi> there, <ns0:hi>for the young Child,</ns0:hi> whom he doth not call <ns0:hi>King,</ns0:hi> thereby dissembling his bloody Mind, and making as if he had no jea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lousie of him, yet withal he suggests to them, that he was like to be a <ns0:hi>Great Prince,</ns0:hi> or else he would never have pre<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tended that he had a Design, when once he knew certainly where he was, to <ns0:hi>go and</ns0:hi> pay <ns0:hi>an Homage to him.</ns0:hi> This Text lets us see the Malignity of <ns0:hi>Herods</ns0:hi> Heart, and indeed of all wicked mens Hearts. <ns0:hi>Herod</ns0:hi> knew that the <ns0:hi>Messiah</ns0:hi> was born. The <ns0:hi>Extraordinary Star,</ns0:hi> and the coming of the <ns0:hi>Wise Men,</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>Priests</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Scribes Answer</ns0:hi> to him could not but confirm him, that he was born, who was long since Pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mised, as a <ns0:hi>King and Governour to Israel,</ns0:hi> yet could he not obtain of his wretched Heart, to comply with the Counsels of God, but contrary to his own Convictions, shews the folly of his Heart, in thinking it was in his Power to <ns0:hi>frustrate the Di<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vine Counsels,</ns0:hi> and be too hard for God himself, nor is his <ns0:hi>folly</ns0:hi> less remarkable, not sending any of his own Courtiers with them, whom he might better have trusted than meer Stran<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gers to have come back, and brought him an account, but whe<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther it was, that he durst not trust any of the <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> or that he was over credulous in trusting to the innocent Simplicity of these Wise Men, being not made acquainted with his In<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tentions he suffereth them to go alone upon this Errand, whom he might possibly think would be least suspected of <ns0:hi>Ioseph</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Mary,</ns0:hi> so as at their return he should have a more full ac<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />count of all Circumstances concerning him, than he could have expected from one who had been taken notice of, as one that belonged to his Court.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="9">9 And when they had heard the King they de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />parted, and lo the Star which they saw in the East, went before them, till it came, and stood over where the young child was.<ns0:note place="bottom">They departed toward <ns0:hi>Bethlehem Iudah,</ns0:hi> how long their Journey was we cannot tell, some wonder, that none of the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> did attend them in their Journey, coming out of their own Country upon such a Discovery, and impute it either to the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> Fear of the <ns0:hi>Tyrant</ns0:hi> under which they were, or to the blindess and hardness of their Hearts, for St. <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> tells us <ns0:hi>he came amongst his own, and they received him not</ns0:hi>; but it is possible that the <ns0:hi>Wise Mens</ns0:hi> immediate Applications were to the <ns0:hi>Court,</ns0:hi> as thinking that the most probable place to hear of one that should be born <ns0:hi>King of the Iews</ns0:hi>; and it may be questioned whether <ns0:hi>Herod,</ns0:hi> tho he called the <ns0:hi>Scribes,</ns0:hi> and the <ns0:hi>Priests</ns0:hi> together told them, that his Summoning of them was occasioned by the coming of the <ns0:hi>Wise Men,</ns0:hi> for the only Question he <ns0:hi>propounded to them,</ns0:hi> was <ns0:hi>where Christ was to be born,</ns0:hi> which they might understand without any Relation to the Wise Mens Question. Nor is it probable that <ns0:hi>Herod</ns0:hi> should be more open than needed in publishing the coming of these <ns0:hi>Wise Men</ns0:hi> or their Errand. Yet, the Text saying that not only <ns0:hi>Herod<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> but all Ierusalem was troubled,</ns0:hi> suggests to us that both their Coming, and the Occasion of it, was noised abroad, more than probably <ns0:hi>Herod</ns0:hi> could have wished, but it is like their Dismission was so private, that if any of the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> had, had an Heart and Courage enough to have gone with them, yet they might not have had Opportunity. It is more admirable, that <ns0:hi>Herod</ns0:hi> sent none that he could securely trust with them. But the hand of God was in this thing. <ns0:hi>They shall be hid whom he will <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>ide.</ns0:hi> The Lord had prepared them a better Guide. The <ns0:hi>Star</ns0:hi> which probably had disappeared for a good time, while they were upon their Journey to <ns0:hi>Ierusalem</ns0:hi> (for they needed no Star to guide them, to so Famous a place) as soon as they were out of <ns0:hi>Ierusalem</ns0:hi> appeared again [<ns0:hi>and went before them, till it came, and stood over where the young Child was</ns0:hi>] probably, the Star appeared in the lower Region, and tho it could not point so directly that they should know the very House, yet it might point so near as by inquiry, they might easily find it, especially by the influence of God upon their Spirits, which doubtless they did not want, whether these Wise Men, were of the Posterity of <ns0:hi>Balaam,</ns0:hi> who Prophes<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ed, <ns0:hi>Num.</ns0:hi> 24.17.19. of a <ns0:hi>Scepter</ns0:hi> that <ns0:hi>should arise out of Israel, that should smite the corners of Moab,</ns0:hi> one that <ns0:hi>should have Domi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nion,</ns0:hi> &c. Or this <ns0:hi>Star</ns0:hi> had any Relation to the Star menti<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />oned there, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 17. is very incertain: It is more probable that these <ns0:hi>Wise Men</ns0:hi> came a far further Journey, and that the <ns0:hi>Star</ns0:hi> there mentioned was not to be understood in a literal Sense, but better expounded by <ns0:hi>Simeon, Luk.</ns0:hi> 2.32. A <ns0:hi>Light to lighten the Gentles and to be the Glory of his People Israel.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="10">10 And when they saw the Star, they rejoyced with exceeding great joy.<ns0:note place="bottom">Joy is but the natural Consequent of Desire satisfied, they had in their own Country seen an extraordinary <ns0:hi>Star,</ns0:hi> which according to the Rules of their own Art, they might guess to be an <ns0:hi>Indication</ns0:hi> of a great <ns0:hi>Prince born</ns0:hi>; or by a <ns0:hi>Divine Reve<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lation</ns0:hi> they might know to be so. This kindled in them a strong Desire, to go and pay an <ns0:hi>Homage</ns0:hi> to him, upon this they take <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>a long Journey to <ns0:hi>Ierusalem.</ns0:hi> When they come there they were more fully confirmed, from the Answer of the <ns0:hi>Priests,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Scribes,</ns0:hi> that there was a <ns0:hi>Christ</ns0:hi> to be born in <ns0:hi>Bethlehem Iudah,</ns0:hi> thither they go, in their Journey, the same <ns0:hi>Star</ns0:hi> they had before seen, appears to them again confirming both their former Apprehensions, and by its standing over <ns0:hi>Bethlehem,</ns0:hi> and a <ns0:hi>particular</ns0:hi> House in it (to their Apprehensions) they were fully confirmed, that they had right Instructions from <ns0:hi>Herod</ns0:hi> and rejoyced in the <ns0:hi>Satisfaction</ns0:hi> of their <ns0:hi>Desires natu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rally,</ns0:hi> and possibly rejoyced <ns0:hi>Spiritually</ns0:hi> in this matter of <ns0:hi>Ioy to all People,</ns0:hi> if they had (as is probable) a <ns0:hi>Spiritual Illumina<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion,</ns0:hi> and believed that this Christ was also <ns0:hi>Iesus,</ns0:hi> one come to save both <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Gentiles from their sins.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="11">11 When they were come into the house, they saw the young child with Mary his Mother, and fell down and worshipped him; and when they had opened their Treasures, they <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>offered.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> presented unto him Gifts, Gold, and Frankincense and Myrrh.<ns0:note place="bottom">How long the <ns0:hi>Virgin Mary,</ns0:hi> and her holy Child had been there, is not expressed, those that think, that these <ns0:hi>Wise Men</ns0:hi> came within six Weeks or two Months, judge that <ns0:hi>Ioseph</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Mary</ns0:hi> came thither from <ns0:hi>Ierusalem</ns0:hi> after that he had been there offered to the Lord, of which you read, <ns0:hi>Luk.</ns0:hi> 2. but they are forced to uphold this to interpret, <ns0:hi>Luk.</ns0:hi> 2.39. which saith, <ns0:hi>That after they had performed all things according to the Law of the Lord,</ns0:hi> they <ns0:hi>returned into Galil<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>e to their own City Nazareth:</ns0:hi> Of a considerable time after they had perform<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed these things which seemeth something hard, and needless, especially considering <ns0:hi>Nazareth</ns0:hi> was <ns0:hi>Iosephs own City<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> i. e.</ns0:hi> The City where his fixed Habitation was: It is most probable, that they after so long absence, went right home, and if the <ns0:hi>Wise Men</ns0:hi> (which is said) found them in <ns0:hi>Bethlehem,</ns0:hi> they were gone thither again to visit some Relations. <ns0:hi>They saw the young Child with Mary his Mother,</ns0:hi> under what other Circumstan<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ces the Scripture saith not, but questionless they were very <ns0:hi>Poor</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Mean,</ns0:hi> which is a very strong inducement to us to be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lieve, that they had a <ns0:hi>Spiritual Divine Revelation.</ns0:hi> That this was a <ns0:hi>King,</ns0:hi> whose <ns0:hi>Kingdom was not of this World,</ns0:hi> the true <ns0:hi>Messiah,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Saviour of the World,</ns0:hi> they would hardly else have treated a poor Infant, in an ordinary House and no more attended, at the <ns0:hi>rate</ns0:hi> they did, for the Text saith [<ns0:hi>they fell down and Worshipped him</ns0:hi>] an usual Homage indeed which the <ns0:hi>Eastern Nations</ns0:hi> paid to <ns0:hi>Princes.</ns0:hi> But they used then to have better Evidences of their <ns0:hi>Royal State</ns0:hi> and Dignity, than these Wise Men seemed to have had, if they had not besides the <ns0:hi>Star</ns0:hi> a Divine <ns0:hi>Revelation,</ns0:hi> what manner of <ns0:hi>King</ns0:hi> this was to be. We may therefore rather judge that their <ns0:hi>Revelation</ns0:hi> extended not only to the Birth of a <ns0:hi>King,</ns0:hi> but of such a King as indeed he was, the Eternal Son of God clothed with humane Flesh; and that their <ns0:hi>falling down</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Worshipping him,</ns0:hi> is to be un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />derstood of a Divine <ns0:hi>Worship</ns0:hi> they paid to him, as the Saviour of the World: And so they were the first Fruits of the <ns0:hi>Gen<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tiles,</ns0:hi> owning, and believing in the Lord Jesus Christ. And that their following Offerings to him were upon that Account, for opening their Treasures, they presented to him <ns0:hi>Gold, Frankin<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cense</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Myrrh,</ns0:hi> the Guesses of those, who think that they offered him <ns0:hi>Gold,</ns0:hi> as to a <ns0:hi>King, Frankincense</ns0:hi> as an <ns0:hi>High Priest,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Myrrh</ns0:hi> to sweeten the place where he was, I take to be but the Product of Luxuriant Fancies. It is most cer<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tain that those <ns0:hi>Eastern</ns0:hi> People, seldom came to their Princes without so<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>e Presents, and that their Presents were usually of the most choice things their Country afforded, This is plain from <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 43. <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 11. and if what Naturalli<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>s tell us be true that <ns0:hi>Myrrh</ns0:hi> was only to be sound in <ns0:hi>Arabia,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Frakincense</ns0:hi> in <ns0:hi>Sabea</ns0:hi> (a part of <ns0:hi>Arabia</ns0:hi>) and that Country also had <ns0:hi>Gold,</ns0:hi> which it is plain that it had, from 2 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 9.14. it makes a very probable Argument, that these <ns0:hi>Wise Men</ns0:hi> came from <ns0:hi>Arabia,</ns0:hi> which was full of Men that were <ns0:hi>Astrologers.</ns0:hi> The Providence of God was wonderfully seen in these Presents, by them providing for the Sustenance of <ns0:hi>Ioseph,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Mary,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Iesus</ns0:hi> in that Exile which they were soon after to indure, for other <ns0:hi>Allegorical</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Mystical</ns0:hi> Significations of these Presents they are but Conjectures, and the Exuberancies of mens Fancies</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="12">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:221" />12 And being, warned of God in a dream, that they should not return to Herod, they depar<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ted into their own Country another way.<ns0:note place="bottom">Now the wise God beginneth to defeat the crafty Counsels of <ns0:hi>Herod,</ns0:hi> whose bloody Hand he had stayed, till he should from the <ns0:hi>Wise Men</ns0:hi> have had a perfect Intelligence, concerning this new born <ns0:hi>King.</ns0:hi> God in a Dream appeareth to the <ns0:hi>Wise Men,</ns0:hi> and warneth them to go no more to <ns0:hi>Herod</ns0:hi> The <ns0:hi>Wise Men</ns0:hi> came with no intention to serve <ns0:hi>Herod</ns0:hi>'s bloody Designs, but came in the <ns0:hi>Simplicity</ns0:hi> of their Hearts: This <ns0:hi>Simp<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>icity</ns0:hi> o<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> theirs, <ns0:hi>Herod</ns0:hi> would have abused, to have made them Accessa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ries to his Guilt. God will not suffer it: <ns0:hi>He who walketh uprightly, walks safely.</ns0:hi> Thus the <ns0:hi>Integrity</ns0:hi> of <ns0:hi>Abimelech</ns0:hi> in taking <ns0:hi>Sarah</ns0:hi> protected him from Guilt with reference to her, <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 20.6. The word which we here translate <ns0:hi>warned of God,</ns0:hi> is used of Persons, whom God is pleased to Honour so far as to Discourse with: Either, <ns0:hi>by himself</ns0:hi>
                     <ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> or <ns0:hi>an Angel<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> Luk.</ns0:hi> 2.26. <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 10.22. <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> 8.5. and 11, 7. Thus hath God honoured these <ns0:hi>Wise Men,</ns0:hi> whose Hearts were inclined to<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />wards him and his <ns0:hi>Christ.</ns0:hi> 1. <ns0:hi>By giving them a Star,</ns0:hi> to guide them. 2. <ns0:hi>Confirming their Hearts by his Word,</ns0:hi> from the Mouths of the chief <ns0:hi>Priests and Scribes,</ns0:hi> that they were not mistaken concerning the Star and its Indication. 3. <ns0:hi>By speaking himself to them,</ns0:hi> to keep them from any Guilt or be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing so much as Accessaries any way to that bloody Tragedy, which upon their departure he knew would be Acted: They take another way to go into their own Country, so we hear o<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> them no more.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="13">13 And when they were departed, Behold the Angel of the Lord appeared to Joseph in a dream, saying, Arise and take the young child, and his mo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther, and flee into Egypt, and be thou there, un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />till I bring thee word, for Herod will seek the young child to destroy it.<ns0:note place="bottom">How long it was before this <ns0:hi>Apparition</ns0:hi> to <ns0:hi>Ioseph,</ns0:hi> the Scripture saith not, but admitting what is affirmed by some <ns0:hi>Geographers,</ns0:hi> that <ns0:hi>Bethlehem Iudah</ns0:hi> was but two days Jour<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ney from <ns0:hi>Ierusalem,</ns0:hi> it cannot be presumed long, for <ns0:hi>Herod</ns0:hi> had (doubtless) quick Intelligence of the Wise Mens motions Here was a second Temptation upon <ns0:hi>Ioseph,</ns0:hi> who was of no great Quality. (a Carpenter) and might have anxious Thoughts how he in <ns0:hi>Egypt</ns0:hi> should maintain himself, his Wife and Child<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> but <ns0:hi>Ioseph</ns0:hi> knew, <ns0:hi>That the Earth was the Lords, and the fulness thereof,</ns0:hi> tho <ns0:hi>Egypt</ns0:hi> therefore was a Land of <ns0:hi>Idolaters,</ns0:hi> and he had no Vi<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ible way of Subsistence there, yet we shall hear that none o<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> these things made him hesitate. <ns0:hi>Egypt</ns0:hi> was near to <ns0:hi>Palestina,</ns0:hi> and the Dominions of another Prince, within which <ns0:hi>Herod</ns0:hi> had nothing to do, <ns0:hi>Ieroboam</ns0:hi> fled thither<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> 1 <ns0:hi>Kin.</ns0:hi> 11.40. and staid there till the Death of <ns0:hi>Solomon</ns0:hi>: Gods precept here, did not only indicate his Care and <ns0:hi>special Providence</ns0:hi> for, and over this <ns0:hi>Holy Child,</ns0:hi> but included a Promise of <ns0:hi>S<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>stenance</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Support,</ns0:hi> for it, and its Parents, and the Lord further assured <ns0:hi>Ioseph,</ns0:hi> that he should not dye in that <ns0:hi>Exile,</ns0:hi> for he would likewise tell him the time when he should come back. <ns0:hi>Christ's</ns0:hi> time to dye was not yet come, and therefore he would have him out of the way, for he who searcheth the Heart, and tryeth the Reins, and knoweth the Thoughts of Man afar off, did know that <ns0:hi>Herod would seek the young Child to destroy him,</ns0:hi> he should but seek it, for God had resolved to preserve it, but he would shew the Malice of his Heart in seeking of it, therefore God commands him to go away, and directeth him whither to go. The certainty of an issue, from the <ns0:hi>Divine Counsels,</ns0:hi> or a <ns0:hi>Divine Revelation,</ns0:hi> ought not to incourage us in the neglect of any rational, and just means for the obtaining of it. Tho God will provide for his Church and People; yet it is his Will they should use all just, and Lawful means for their own Preservation.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="14">14 When he arose, he took the young child, and his mother by night, and departed into Egypt.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="15">15 And was there until the death of Herod, that it might be fulfilled, which was spoken of the Lord, by the Prophet. Out of Egypt have I called my Son.<ns0:note place="bottom">True <ns0:hi>Faith,</ns0:hi> or assent to a <ns0:hi>Divine Revelation;</ns0:hi> always pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />duceth <ns0:hi>Obedience</ns0:hi> to the Precept of it. Thus it did in the Wise Men, thus in <ns0:hi>Ioseph,</ns0:hi> thus every were in Holy-writ: By which we may learn. That they indeed believe not the Scrip<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tures to be the word of God, who take no Care to live up to the rule of Life prescribed in them. <ns0:hi>Ioseph</ns0:hi> not only obeyed but <ns0:hi>readi<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>y,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>presently</ns0:hi> obeyed: <ns0:hi>When he arose he took the young Child,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Mary his Mother.</ns0:hi> The Poverty of our Saviours Parents is not obscurely gathered from this hasty mo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion of <ns0:hi>Ioseph.</ns0:hi> His motion was not delayed for the Packing up of Goods, gathering in of Debts, &c. if he lost any thing by his haste, yet he carried with him, the Promise and special Care of God for him, and his; yet he moveth <ns0:hi>Prudentially,</ns0:hi> and therefore he beginneth his Journey <ns0:hi>by Night,</ns0:hi> when least notice could be taken of his motion. We are not to put God upon working Miracles for our Preservation, tho we have ne<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ver so many sure Promises, when it may he obtained in the use of means. They are Gods Security given to Creatures, whom he hath indued with reason, and express that we should use it, while we yet trust in his word. We are not told into what part of <ns0:hi>Egypt Ioseph</ns0:hi> went, nor how long he <ns0:hi>staid</ns0:hi> there: Some say six or seven years, others, but three or four Months. The Text saith: <ns0:hi>He was there untill the Death of Herod</ns0:hi>
                     <ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> some say that was before the <ns0:hi>Paschal Solemnity</ns0:hi> that year. But these things are great incertainties. It is certain he staid there till <ns0:hi>Herod</ns0:hi> dyed, but when that certainly was, we know not, nor is it material for us to be Curious in inquiring. [<ns0:hi>That it might be fulfilled, which was spoken of the Lord by the Prophet. Out of Egypt have I called my Son</ns0:hi>] That it might be fulfilled is a Phrase we often meet with in the <ns0:hi>New Testament,</ns0:hi> to declare the Har<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mony of Scripture, and the Faithfulness of God, in fulfilling the <ns0:hi>Prophesies,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Promises</ns0:hi> of the Old Testament. <ns0:hi>Spanhe<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mius</ns0:hi> tells us, The Scripture is said to be fulfilled <ns0:hi>Properly</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>improperly. Properly</ns0:hi> two ways, either <ns0:hi>Literally</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Mystically, Improperly, Secondarily,</ns0:hi> when some suck like thing hap'neth, as was before foretold or spoken of, or an <ns0:hi>Example</ns0:hi> is brought Paralel to some former Example. <ns0:hi>Literally</ns0:hi> the Scripture is said to be fulfilled. 1. When a thing before Prophecied of, or Promised, cometh to pass. Thus <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 1.22. the Prophecy <ns0:hi>Isaiah</ns0:hi> 7.14. was Literally fulfilled, so <ns0:hi>Micah</ns0:hi> 5.2. was Li<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />terally fulfilled, <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 2.6. by Christ's being born in <ns0:hi>Bethle<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />hem,</ns0:hi> so <ns0:hi>Zech.</ns0:hi> 9.9. was Literally fulfilled, <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 21.5. Or else. 2. <ns0:hi>When the Type is fulfilled in the Antitype.</ns0:hi> Thus we read of many Scriptures of the Old Testament fulfilled in Christ, se<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />veral things about the <ns0:hi>Paschal Lamb,</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>Brasen Serpent, So<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lomon, David, Ionas,</ns0:hi> &c. <ns0:hi>Improperly</ns0:hi> the Scripture is said to be fulfilled: When any thing is reported as done, which <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                        <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> a Proportion to something before recorded in Holy-writ, as <ns0:hi>spoken</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>done,</ns0:hi> thus Christ applieth the same thing to the Hy<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pocrites which lived in his time, which <ns0:hi>Isaiah</ns0:hi> spake of those who lived in his time, <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 29.13. <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 15.7, 8. so 13, 14. <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 6.9. this Divines call a <ns0:hi>Fulfilling, per Accomo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dationem, aut Transumptionem.</ns0:hi> The Question is, whether this Scripture which is, <ns0:hi>Hosea</ns0:hi> 11.1. was fulfilled in <ns0:hi>Christ's</ns0:hi> being carried into <ns0:hi>Egypt, Properly</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Improperly</ns0:hi>: There is a great Variety of Opinions, those possibly judge best who think that the <ns0:hi>Israelites</ns0:hi> going into, and coming out of <ns0:hi>Egypt,</ns0:hi> was a Type of Christ's going into <ns0:hi>Egypt,</ns0:hi> being preserved there and coming out again, <ns0:hi>Matthew</ns0:hi> saith <ns0:hi>the Scripture was fulfilled,</ns0:hi> whether <ns0:hi>Properly</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Improperly,</ns0:hi> is not much mate<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rial for us to know, I have only added thus much to shorten my Discourse hereafter where we shall meet with this Phrase.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="16">16 Then Herod when he saw he was mock<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed of the wise men, was exceeding wroth and sent forth, and slew all the Children which were in Bethlehem, and in all the Coasts thereof from two years old and under<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> according to the time which he had diligently inquired of the wise men.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Herod</ns0:hi> now expounds what he meant by his coming and <ns0:hi>Worshipping Christ also,</ns0:hi> which he talked of <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 8. <ns0:hi>When he saw that he was mocked,</ns0:hi> &c. really mocked by their com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing no more to him, not that they used any mocking Lan<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />guage, or designed by their Actions to deceive him, but Pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bably intended to have gone back according to his Desire, but that they were otherwise admonished by God in a Dream. [<ns0:hi>He was exceeding wroth</ns0:hi>] as great Persons use to be when they see any great Design, they have, frustrated by their Inferiors [<ns0:hi>and sent forth and slew all the Children in Bethlehem, and in the Coasts thereof from two years old, and under</ns0:hi>] he sent forth Soldiers, or Executioners and slew <ns0:hi>all the Children,</ns0:hi> there is a Tradition that amongst them he <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>lew his own Son, and that <ns0:hi>Augustus Caesar</ns0:hi> hearing it<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> should say, <ns0:hi>It was better to be Herods Hog than his Child,</ns0:hi> because the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> will eat no Swines flesh. Others say this is but a <ns0:hi>Fable,</ns0:hi> for his Son died very few days before himself, from two years old and under. If we take these words as they seem to sound, they would incline us to think that Christ was near two years old before the Wise Men came, but some very learned Men think they came within a year or little more, and that the term we translate <ns0:hi>two years old,</ns0:hi> signifieth Persons that had never so little entred upon the second year of their Age: So as if a Child were but a year and a Week old, he was Pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />perly enough called <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, one of two years old, that is who had began his <ns0:hi>second year.</ns0:hi> Hence they think that the <ns0:hi>Star</ns0:hi> appeared some little matter above a year before they came to <ns0:hi>Bethlehem,</ns0:hi> and considering at how great distance some parts in <ns0:hi>Arabia</ns0:hi> were from <ns0:hi>Ierusalem,</ns0:hi> they think that a year might well be ran out in their Deliberations about, and Preparations for, and dispatch of their Journey. Thus they interpret the next words [<ns0:hi>according to the time he had dili<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gently inquired of the Wise Men</ns0:hi>] that they had told them, that it was something above a year, since the Star appeared first. This is now a middle way, betwixt those who (very impro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bably) think that they came within thirteen days, too short a time doubtless for such a Journey, and those that think they came not till near two years, which to some seemeth as much too long. I leave it to the Readers judgment.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="17">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:221" />17 Then was fulfilled that which was spoken by Jeremy the Prophet saying.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="18">18 In Rama was there a voice heard, lamen<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tation and weeping, and great mourning, Rachel weeping for her children, and would not be com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />forted, because they are not.<ns0:note place="bottom">The Text quoted, is <ns0:hi>Ier.</ns0:hi> 31.15. this Prophecy was literally fulfilled when <ns0:hi>Iudah</ns0:hi> was carried into Captivity: There was then a great mourning in the Tribes of <ns0:hi>Benjamin</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Iudah,</ns0:hi> for their Children that were slain and carried into Captivity: It was now <ns0:hi>fulfilled,</ns0:hi> that is, verified a second time. There is no need that <ns0:hi>Rama</ns0:hi> here should be taken <ns0:hi>Appellatively,</ns0:hi> as it sig<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nifieth an <ns0:hi>High place,</ns0:hi> from whence a noise is most loudly, and dolefully heard. There were several places so named, one near <ns0:hi>Bethlehem</ns0:hi> (formerly called <ns0:hi>Ephran) Gen.</ns0:hi> 35.16.19 <ns0:hi>Iud.</ns0:hi> 4.5. a City in the lot of <ns0:hi>Benjamin, Ios.</ns0:hi> 18.22. The slaughter was in <ns0:hi>Bethlehem</ns0:hi> and the Coasts thereof, the noise reached to <ns0:hi>Rama</ns0:hi> which was close by, both <ns0:hi>Benjamin,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Iudah</ns0:hi> made up the one Kingdom of <ns0:hi>Iudah. Rachel</ns0:hi> was the Mother of <ns0:hi>Benjamin,</ns0:hi> a Woman pa<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="3 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>•••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>onately desirous of Children, therefore the fittest Person to have her name used, to express the sorrow of all those Mothers, who had lost their Children in this slaughter. The slaughter of these Children caused a lamentable Mourning by tender Mothers throughout <ns0:hi>Benjamin</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Iudah,</ns0:hi> such as the former Captivity caused to be mentioned, <ns0:hi>Ier.</ns0:hi> 31.15.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="19">19 But when Herod was dead, behold, an An<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gel of the Lord appeared in a dream to Joseph in Egypt;</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="20">20 Saying arise, and take the young child, and his mother and go into the land of Israel, for they are dead who sought the young childs life.<ns0:note place="bottom">That is, as some say, within three or four Months (for <ns0:hi>Herod</ns0:hi> they say no longer out-lived this bloody Act) and if we may believe Historians, he was in his Death, made a dread<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ful Example of Divine Vengeance, but we cannot assert the just time how long he out-lived this bloody Act; when he was dead, God who had promised <ns0:hi>Ioseph v.</ns0:hi> 13. to tell him by an <ns0:hi>Angel</ns0:hi> (as before) let <ns0:hi>Ioseph</ns0:hi> know he might safely return: It is probable this Apparition was not immediately upon the Death of <ns0:hi>Herod,</ns0:hi> for <ns0:hi>Archelaus</ns0:hi> was reigning, who must be allowed some time to go to <ns0:hi>Rome,</ns0:hi> and to have this <ns0:hi>Dignity</ns0:hi> conferred on him, but soon after he was Dead, this <ns0:hi>Apparition</ns0:hi> was, with a Command to him, to return into the Land of <ns0:hi>Israel,</ns0:hi> to which he soon yieldeth Obedience.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="21">21 And he arose, and took the young child, and his mother, and came into the Land of Israel.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="22">22 But when he heard that Archelaus did reign in Judea in the room of his father Herod, he was afraid to go thither: Notwithstanding being warn<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ned of God in a dream, he turned aside into the parts of Galilee.<ns0:note place="bottom">The true King of the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> being born, The singular <ns0:hi>Pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vidence</ns0:hi> of God so ordered it, that there were no more con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stituted Governours of <ns0:hi>Iudea,</ns0:hi> under the Title of <ns0:hi>Kings,</ns0:hi> tho they are said to Reign, because the <ns0:hi>Tetrarchs</ns0:hi> in their Provinces, exercised a <ns0:hi>Regal-Power</ns0:hi>: For tho <ns0:hi>Archelaus</ns0:hi> was by his Fa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thers Will declared his Successor in the Kingdom, yet the <ns0:hi>Emperour</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Senate</ns0:hi> of <ns0:hi>Rome</ns0:hi> was to confirm him, who made <ns0:hi>Archelaus Tetrarch</ns0:hi> of <ns0:hi>Iudea,</ns0:hi> as appears by this <ns0:hi>Chap. Antipas</ns0:hi> another of his Sons, called also by his Fathers name, <ns0:hi>Tetrarch</ns0:hi> of <ns0:hi>Galilee, Philip,</ns0:hi> another of his Sons, <ns0:hi>Tetrarch of Iturea,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Lysanias Tetrarch</ns0:hi> of <ns0:hi>Abylene</ns0:hi> and set a <ns0:hi>Governour</ns0:hi> over <ns0:hi>Iudea</ns0:hi> which was <ns0:hi>Pontius Pilate,</ns0:hi> as appeareth by <ns0:hi>Luk.</ns0:hi> 3.1. of all the Sons of <ns0:hi>Herod, Archelaus</ns0:hi> is said to be of the most fierce, and bloody Disposition, which made <ns0:hi>Ioseph</ns0:hi> afraid to go thither. His Brother <ns0:hi>Herod Antipas</ns0:hi> is reported of a much milder Disposition, and more in<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />active Temper; so <ns0:hi>Ioseph</ns0:hi> not without the Direction of God goeth into his own <ns0:hi>Province</ns0:hi> which was <ns0:hi>Galilee.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="23">23 And he came and dwelt in a City called Nazareth, that it might be fulfilled which was spo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ken by the Prophets, he shall be called a Nazarene.<ns0:note place="bottom">It appeareth by <ns0:hi>Luk.</ns0:hi> 2.4. That <ns0:hi>Ioseph</ns0:hi> dwelt in <ns0:hi>Naza<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />reth,</ns0:hi> before our Saviour was born, and <ns0:hi>Luk.</ns0:hi> 2.39. after <ns0:hi>Maries Purification</ns0:hi> it is said, <ns0:hi>They returned into Galilee, to their own City Nazareth</ns0:hi>
                     <ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> and <ns0:hi>Luk.</ns0:hi> 4.16. he was there <ns0:hi>brought up.</ns0:hi> Hence <ns0:hi>Ioh.</ns0:hi> 1.45. he is called by <ns0:hi>Philip Iesus of Nazareth,</ns0:hi> but the following words of this Verse afford as great Difficul<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ties as any other in Holy-writ. 1. <ns0:hi>How Christ could be called a Nazarene,</ns0:hi> who apparently was born at <ns0:hi>Bethlehem.</ns0:hi> 2. <ns0:hi>How the Evangelist saith that was fulfilled which was spoken by the Prophet, he shall be called a Nazarene:</ns0:hi> When as there is no such saying in all the <ns0:hi>Prophets.</ns0:hi> There is a strange Va<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />riety of Opinions as to these Questions, <ns0:hi>Spanhemius</ns0:hi> acquies<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ceth in that which seemeth least liable to Exception, <ns0:hi>viz.</ns0:hi> That Christ was to put a Period to that Order of <ns0:hi>Nazarites,</ns0:hi> amongst the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> whose Rules we have <ns0:hi>Num.</ns0:hi> 6.2, 3. of which Order <ns0:hi>Samson</ns0:hi> was, as appears by <ns0:hi>Iud.</ns0:hi> 13.7. and <ns0:hi>Ioseph</ns0:hi> was called <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> 
                     <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 49.26. the very same word which is used <ns0:hi>Iud.</ns0:hi> 13.7. Both <ns0:hi>Ioseph</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Samson</ns0:hi> were eminent Types of Christ. And it was spoken of Christ by the Prophets (the Holy men of God who wrote the Scriptures) that Christ should be called <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> 
                     <ns0:hi>Nezir,</ns0:hi> as it is in the <ns0:hi>Hebrew,</ns0:hi> in that it was spoken of those that were his Types; who are both express<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly so called. The word signifieth an Holy Person, one separated to God, and from ordinary converse with Men, Christ was to be such a <ns0:hi>Nazarite,</ns0:hi> separated to God, for the accom<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />plishment of our Redemption, and like <ns0:hi>Ioseph</ns0:hi> separated from his <ns0:hi>Brethren, Isa.</ns0:hi> 53.3. he was <ns0:hi>rejected of Men:—We hid as it were our Faces from him, and we esteemed him not.</ns0:hi> God by his singular Providence so ordered it, that he who was the <ns0:hi>Antitype</ns0:hi> to all the <ns0:hi>Nazarites,</ns0:hi> and the true <ns0:hi>Nezir</ns0:hi> or Person separated, should be Educated at <ns0:hi>Nazareth,</ns0:hi> a poor Contemp<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tible Town, <ns0:hi>Io.</ns0:hi> 1.46. <ns0:hi>Nathaniel said, can there any Good come out</ns0:hi> of <ns0:hi>Nazareth</ns0:hi>? That while his Education there gave the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> an occasion to reproach him, as a <ns0:hi>Nazarene</ns0:hi>; because born at <ns0:hi>Nazareth,</ns0:hi> believers amongst the <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> might under<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stand him to be the true <ns0:hi>Nazarite,</ns0:hi> understood in <ns0:hi>Ioseph</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Samson</ns0:hi> called by this name, as Types and Figures of him who was to come, <ns0:hi>separated by God</ns0:hi> to a more Excellent end, and <ns0:hi>from Men</ns0:hi> in a more Eminent manner. So that what the <ns0:hi>Prophets</ns0:hi> spake of this Nature concerning Christ, they spake of those who were the true Types of Christ. Those who will read <ns0:hi>Spanhemius,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Pooli Critica,</ns0:hi> will find large Dis<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />courses about the Difficulties of this Text, but this seemeth to be <ns0:hi>Spanhemius</ns0:hi> his Opinion, improving the Notion of Mr. <ns0:hi>Calvin.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>
